title: Burying Feature Flags in Hot Execution Paths
pattern: Evaluating feature flags or dynamic configuration lookups inside tight, CPU-bound execution loops or low-level parser runs.
why_bad: Introduces severe performance regressions. Frequent string-based hash maps or atomic lookups inside tight loops disrupt cache alignment, disable compiler loop-unrolling, and burn unnecessary CPU cycles.
detection: Evaluation of configuration variables or string keys within high-frequency loops or recursion pipelines.
fix: Evaluate configurations once outside performance-critical pathways; select the correct processing strategy loop before handling bulk transactions.
source: Titus Winters, Tom Manshreck, Hyrum Wright - *Software Engineering at Google_ Lessons Learned from Programming Over Time* (2020, O'Reilly Media).pdf, Chapter 24; Kent Beck - *Tidy First?* (2023, O'Reilly Media).pdf, Chapter 28.
